This is as a result of the “Mercator projection”. On a Mercator map, the straight lines represented constant compass bearings. That meant sailors could chart a course across the ocean without recalculating their path, which, as you could imagine, was a huge deal in the year 1569! For navigation, a Mercator map is the perfect map to plan your course. 

But for understanding the actual size of countries and continents, it’s not ideal. To put a round planet on a flat page, you must “squash” and “stretch” something to make it fit. The Mercator projection ends up distorting the land as it moves toward the poles, making places like Europe and North America look larger than they are, and making countries closer to the equator appear much smaller. 

That’s why Greenland looks gigantic next to Africa on a Mercator map, even though Africa is over 14x larger in reality! It’s also why mapmakers often say: choose the right map for the story you want to tell. 

All maps attempt to present the curved Earth (yes, it's round!) on a flat piece of paper, which will always result in some compromise and distortion. 

→ So, if you want to compare land size, use an Equal-Earth projection map. 
→ But if you want to navigate the seven seas, Mercator projection has got you covered! 

Want to see the TRUE size of countries around the world for yourself? This website lets you overlay any country you choose onto an equal-projection map to compare the real size!  →
https://lnkd.in/eiUMaPHh

Built on behalf of Tiakina Kauri - the national Kauri protection programme based in Biosecurity New Zealand, Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI), and in partnership with mana whenua and other agencies, Kete Aronui was recognised as a leading example of how groups can work together to share data securely and support better decision-making. 

Kauri are a taonga of Aotearoa, growing naturally in Northland, Auckland, Coromandel, Waikato and the Bay of Plenty, and are threatened by Phytophthora agathidicida (PA), a soil-borne pathogen. Kete Aronui brings together data and tools to track the spread of PA and Kauri locations at a national level. 🗺️

PA spreads through soil movement on dirty footwear, clothing, equipment, vehicles, and animals moving through infected areas. It infects trees through their roots, blocking the flow of water and nutrients. Over time, this starves the tree and eventually kills it.
 
Protecting Kauri for future generations depends on all of us. By cleaning your gear and staying on marked tracks you can help protect Kauri. 🤝

Learn more about protecting Kauri: www.kauriprotection.co.nz

Google has just released a new voice for Maps users in New Zealand, which speaks English with a Kiwi accent while accurately pronouncing te reo Māori place and street names.

This is a rare opportunity for an internationally experienced hydrographic leader to guide one of the world's most geographically diverse and strategically significant programmes.

As New Zealand's recognised authority on hydrography, you will lead our nautical charting and hydrographic programme, supporting safe navigation across New Zealand waters, five Pacific Island countries, and the Ross Sea in Antarctica.

Why this role matters: 🛟 
Every voyage, port movement, and maritime decision depends on trusted hydrographic information. Your leadership will directly support:
- Safety of life at sea
- Resilient supply chains
- Environmental stewardship
- Economic prosperity across New Zealand and the South West Pacific

What you'll lead: 🛟 
You'll operate at the intersection of science, technology, and international collaboration, including:
- Setting national direction and delivery for hydrography, leading surveying, seabed and coastal mapping, and chart production
- Driving digital transformation through the transition to the S‑100 ecosystem
- Providing trusted advice to government and regulators on navigation safety and marine policy
- Building strong partnerships across ports, harbourmasters, iwi, pilots, and industry
- Strengthening Pacific capability to support regional safety and resilience
- Representing New Zealand regionally and globally through the South West Pacific Hydrographic Commission and the International Hydrographic Organization (IHO)

Who we're looking for: 🛟 
An internationally respected hydrographer with the credibility and leadership to operate at the highest levels. You'll bring:
- Deep technical expertise in hydrography and maritime geospatial information
- Experience in a national hydrographic office or equivalent maritime authority
- Experience influencing senior government and industry stakeholders
- A strong international outlook and ability to represent New Zealand globally
- A commitment to collaboration, partnership, and public value

We welcome applications from experienced hydrographic leaders in New Zealand and internationally. If you're ready for a role with real impact and international standing, apply now or reach out for a confidential conversation.

👉 https://lnkd.in/eWQ4twNR

","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/toit%C5%AB-te-whenua-linz-_hey-there-queenstown-new-aerial-imagery-activity-7478239774596644864-fU3H"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"Organization","name":"Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/toit%C5%AB-te-whenua-linz-","address":{"type":"PostalAddress","streetAddress":"Level 7, Radio New Zealand House","addressLocality":"Wellington","postalCode":"6145","addressCountry":"NZ"},"description":"Our data and expertise underpins New Zealand’s economy and the wellbeing of our communities. Our property survey and title system, on which all New Zealand land ownership and development is based, is world leading. We’re also experts at managing land and property for New Zealand.

Our challenge is to get more people using more of our data when making vital decisions about NZ’s future– whether that’s rebuilding a city, planning for sea level rise or managing our iconic high country.

Our values are Bold, Expert and Stronger Together. That’s the way we work to bring our BEST to New Zealand’s success.

We need people who are bold, unafraid to learn, try new things and get results.

      <div class="core-section-container__content break-words">
        

          <p class="break-words text-color-text" data-test-id="about-us__description">
              Our data and expertise underpins New Zealand’s economy and the wellbeing of our communities. It enables government, businesses and communities to make a whole range of decisions that make a powerful difference to people’s lives.

We’re specialists in geographic information – the data that tells people where things are in the world, on land or under the sea. Our property survey and title system, on which all New Zealand land ownership and development is based, is world leading. We’re also experts at managing land and property for New Zealand.

Our challenge is to get more people using more of our data when making vital decisions about NZ’s future– whether that’s rebuilding a city, planning for sea level rise or managing our iconic high country.

Our values are Bold, Expert and Stronger Together. That’s the way we work to bring our BEST to New Zealand’s success.

We need people who are bold, unafraid to learn, try new things and get results. 
We need people who are passionate about connecting their expertise and knowledge with others. We believe we make more difference when we work with others and support each other.

Our people join us from many backgrounds. We support and back them to build careers and expertise in a whole range of fields, many of which are unique to Toitū Te Whenua – from geospatial science, hydrography and topography to property law, valuation and surveying; from data analytics to iwi relations, public land management, policy and corporate.
          </p>

  <div class="attributed-text-segment-list__container relative mt-1 mb-1.5 babybear:mt-0 babybear:mb-0.5">
    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Ever wondered why on some maps New Zealand looks like a tiny footnote at the bottom of a globe, but in the real world, it's as long as the distance from Denmark to Italy? 🌏🤯 

This is as a result of the “Mercator projection”. On a Mercator map, the straight lines represented constant compass bearings. That meant sailors could chart a course across the ocean without recalculating their path, which, as you could imagine, was a huge deal in the year 1569! For navigation, a Mercator map is the perfect map to plan your course. 

But for understanding the actual size of countries and continents, it’s not ideal. To put a round planet on a flat page, you must “squash” and “stretch” something to make it fit. The Mercator projection ends up distorting the land as it moves toward the poles, making places like Europe and North America look larger than they are, and making countries closer to the equator appear much smaller. 

That’s why Greenland looks gigantic next to Africa on a Mercator map, even though Africa is over 14x larger in reality! It’s also why mapmakers often say: choose the right map for the story you want to tell. 

All maps attempt to present the curved Earth (yes, it's round!) on a flat piece of paper, which will always result in some compromise and distortion. 

→ So, if you want to compare land size, use an Equal-Earth projection map. 
→ But if you want to navigate the seven seas, Mercator projection has got you covered! 

Want to see the TRUE size of countries around the world for yourself? This website lets you overlay any country you choose onto an equal-projection map to compare the real size!  →

📸 Map comparison image source: Weiyi Cai from The New York Times</p>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Kete Aronui, a platform built by LINZ to help protect Aotearoa’s iconic Kauri trees, received a Special Achievement in GIS Award at the Esri User Conference in San Diego on 13 July. 🌳💚

Built on behalf of Tiakina Kauri - the national Kauri protection programme based in Biosecurity New Zealand, <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/new-zealand-ministry-for-primary-industries?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI)</a>, and in partnership with mana whenua and other agencies, Kete Aronui was recognised as a leading example of how groups can work together to share data securely and support better decision-making. 

Kauri are a taonga of Aotearoa, growing naturally in Northland, Auckland, Coromandel, Waikato and the Bay of Plenty, and are threatened by Phytophthora agathidicida (PA), a soil-borne pathogen. Kete Aronui brings together data and tools to track the spread of PA and Kauri locations at a national level. 🗺️

PA spreads through soil movement on dirty footwear, clothing, equipment, vehicles, and animals moving through infected areas. It infects trees through their roots, blocking the flow of water and nutrients. Over time, this starves the tree and eventually kills it.
 
Protecting Kauri for future generations depends on all of us. By cleaning your gear and staying on marked tracks you can help protect Kauri. 🤝

Learn more about protecting Kauri: <a class="link" href="http://www.kauriprotection.co.nz?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>www.kauriprotection.co.nz</a>
</p>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">This Matariki, explore the stories woven into the place names of New Zealand ✨

The stars of Matariki each have their own connection to the natural world- from Waitī and freshwater, Waitā and the oceans, to Ururangi and the winds, and Pōhutukawa, the star associated with remembrance. These same connections can be found in many of the place names that shape our mountains, rivers, lakes, coastlines and communities.

Did you know there's also a locality named Matariki in Nelson, Matariki Falls near Mount Ngauruhoe and Matariki Bay in the Coromandel, all likely named after the star cluster that marks the Māori New Year? ⭐🏔️

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">If you’ve used Google Maps this week you will have noticed a very special update to the pronunciation of New Zealand’s te reo Māori place and street names 🗺️👀

<a class="link" href="https://www.linkedin.com/company/google?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Google</a> has just released a new voice for Maps users in New Zealand, which speaks English with a Kiwi accent while accurately pronouncing te reo Māori place and street names.

A huge mihi goes to <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/te-taura-whiri-i-te-reo-m%C4%81ori?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Te Taura Whiri i te Reo Māori</a> for their leadership and expertise bringing this important mahi to life 👏

Here at LINZ we’ve had heaps of feedback over the years on how much the correct pronunciation of our place names matters to New Zealanders. 

Google Maps pronunciation approach was developed in partnership with Te Taura Whiri and used publicly available data from the NZ Gazetteer produced by Ngā Pou Taunaha o Aotearoa New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB) to help build the new voice.

Place names are taonga, carrying stories, identity and whakapapa. Hearing them spoken correctly helps ensure those meanings are understood, respected and shared. So it’s a genuinely exciting step to see Google Maps now pronounce te reo Māori place and street names with greater accuracy 🎉

Want to brush up on your te reo place names? Explore the NZGB’s Gazetteer and listen to more than 9,000 audio clips: <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/gyPvf3pS?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/gyPvf3pS</a>

And read more coverage about this massive milestone for place names and te reo Māori revitalisation in Aotearoa New Zealand:

<a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/waateanews?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Waatea NEWS</a> - <a class="link" href="https://lnkd.in/epB25iDA?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" rel="nofollow" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>https://lnkd.in/epB25iDA</a>

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">That’s a wrap on season two of 3D Coastal Mapping. 

Since October last year, planes and boats have been busy capturing detailed data along our coastline. ✈️🚤

LiDAR capture for this season has been completed across Gisborne, Otago, Southland, Taranaki, Tasman, Waikato, West Coast, Whanganui and parts of Auckland. Discovery Marine Limited (DML) completed multibeam mapping of areas where murky water limited LiDAR coverage, revealing some interesting geological features in stunning detail. We’ve also hit a big milestone, releasing 118 billion classified point cloud points. 🗺️

Together, the data is helping communities, councils and iwi better understand coastal hazards and make informed decisions about the places people live, work and care for.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Role opportunity: National Hydrographer – Shape hydrography across New Zealand, the South West Pacific, and beyond. ⚓

As New Zealand's recognised authority on hydrography, you will lead our nautical charting and hydrographic programme, supporting safe navigation across New Zealand waters, five Pacific Island countries, and the Ross Sea in Antarctica.

Why this role matters: 🛟 
Every voyage, port movement, and maritime decision depends on trusted hydrographic information. Your leadership will directly support:
- Safety of life at sea
- Resilient supply chains
- Environmental stewardship
- Economic prosperity across New Zealand and the South West Pacific

What you'll lead: 🛟

- Setting national direction and delivery for hydrography, leading surveying, seabed and coastal mapping, and chart production
- Driving digital transformation through the transition to the S‑100 ecosystem
- Providing trusted advice to government and regulators on navigation safety and marine policy
- Building strong partnerships across ports, harbourmasters, iwi, pilots, and industry
- Strengthening Pacific capability to support regional safety and resilience

Who we're looking for: 🛟 
An internationally respected hydrographer with the credibility and leadership to operate at the highest levels. You'll bring:
- Deep technical expertise in hydrography and maritime geospatial information

- Experience influencing senior government and industry stakeholders
- A strong international outlook and ability to represent New Zealand globally
